name.text: Angles between the edges of a pyramid

questiontext.text:
VABCD is a right pyramid on a rectangular base with AB = {@ll@} cm and BC = {@ww@} cm. Its height VO is {@hh@} cm.

Find

(a) angle AVC

[[input:ans1]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) angle {@adj@}

[[input:ans2]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

Give lengths correct to 2 decimal places and angles correct to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the final answer.

generalfeedback.text:
(a) \(\mathrm{OA}^2 = \frac{{@ll@}^2 + {@ww@}^2}{4} = {@SA@}\). Triangle VOA has a right angle at O, so \(\tan \mathrm{AVO} = \frac{\mathrm{OA}}{\mathrm{VO}} = \frac{\sqrt{{@SA@}}}{{@hh@}}\), angle AVO = \({@d2(avo)@}^\circ\), and angle AVC = \(2 \times\) angle AVO = \({@d1(t1)@}^\circ\).

(b) \(\mathrm{VA}^2 = \mathrm{VB}^2 = \mathrm{VC}^2 = {@SA@} + {@hh@}^2 = {@SV@}\). In triangle {@face@} the side opposite V is {@sn@} = {@ss@} cm, so \(\cos {@adj@} = \frac{{@SV@} + {@SV@} - {@ss@}^2}{2 \times {@SV@}}\) and angle {@adj@} = \({@d1(t2)@}^\circ\).

questiondescription.text:
Three-Dimensional Geometry: angles between the edges of a pyramid

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.4: Find the angle between opposite sloping edges and between neighbouring sloping edges of a rectangular-based right pyramid.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 7, Exercise C, question 4(b) of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: by calculation instead of drawing, rectangular bases, neighbouring edges added, new numbers, randomised, with named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: okr: is(ans1 > 0 and ans1 < 180); rdn: float(ans1*%pi/180); hf: float(ans1/2); oav: if okr then float(hh*tan(rdn/2)) else NA;

truefeedback.text: That is angle AVO, half of AVC: VO bisects angle AVC.
You doubled angle VAO, the angle at the base. Angle AVC is at V: \(\tan \mathrm{AVO} = \frac{\mathrm{OA}}{\mathrm{VO}}\).
Your calculator is set to radians. Set it to degrees (DEG) and work out the angle again.
Your answer is close but not accurate to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the end, then round the angle once.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="okr"]]

VO bisects angle AVC, so half of your angle, \({@d1(hf)@}^\circ\), would be angle AVO. Triangle VOA has a right angle at O with VO = {@hh@} cm, so that makes OA = {@d2(oav)@} cm. Is that half the diagonal of the base?

[[else]]

An angle of a triangle is between \(0^\circ\) and \(180^\circ\). Check your working and your calculator mode.

[[/if]]

feedbackvariables.text: okr: is(ans2 > 0 and ans2 < 180); rdn: float(ans2*%pi/180); opv: if okr then float(2*sqrt(SV)*sin(rdn/2)) else NA;

truefeedback.text: That is angle {@oadj@}, between the edges at the ends of {@on@}. Angle {@adj@} is opposite {@sn@}, which is {@ss@} cm.
You used the diagonal AC, which gives angle AVC again.

node.description: VO as the height of the face

truefeedback.text: VO is not in the face {@face@}; the triangle {@face@} has no right angle at the foot of VO. Find VA, then use the cosine rule with {@sn@} = {@ss@} cm.
Your calculator is set to radians. Set it to degrees (DEG) and work out the angle again.
Your answer is close but not accurate to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the end, then round the angle once.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="okr"]]

Triangle {@face@} is isosceles: its two sloping edges are equal, each the hypotenuse of a triangle like VOA. With the correct sloping edge and your angle at V, the side opposite V would be {@d2(opv)@} cm, but {@sn@} = {@ss@} cm. Check the sloping edge, then use the cosine rule in triangle {@face@}.

[[else]]

An angle of a triangle is between \(0^\circ\) and \(180^\circ\). Check your working and your calculator mode.

[[/if]]
